confirmed_code_behaviors.finding: Triggered ordinary reanswer replaces answer_choice and explanation; all other complete F fields retained. No reaggregation or second judge.

F appends exact current NLI question and RULE defining entire-hypothesis entailment; ordinary control appends generic question answering plus intact legal data, but not the F-specific RULE/current-question wrapper. Original context remains intact.
Each A/B score vector is finite-checked, peak-subtracted softmaxed, mapped back by displayed names, and averaged. No source/gold key used; tie order follows native key order.
Exact JSON/native key vote; three identical keys stops; tie earliest sample; returned native response is entire selected raw sample.
New answer can retain prior errors/auxiliary values, as predeclared. Any semantic mismatch between changed answer and old auxiliary values requires actual sample review.
At least two distinct semantic keys among existing F predictions triggers; no confidence/net-benefit computation, no gold.
Answer key scored by unchanged AST-loaded native parse/score; robustness errors are separately measured. No gold import in the F inference branch.

mechanism_hypotheses_needing_samples: Replacing an existing multi-path aggregate by one fresh answer may discard a correct selection; count actual repair/harm before attributing cause.
A generic reanswer may interpret NLI positive/negative differently without the old appended entailment definition; look for actual relation/entailment readings, not just changed labels.
Retained auxiliary errors may remain appropriate or conflict with a changed answer; do not infer inconsistency from a field being retained.
NLI score-distribution winners and generated full-native response votes are different objects; do not sum them as equal independent samples.
still_unknown: No static source review alone determines actual medical fact misreading or causal reason for a repair/harm.
Historical file locks do not cover every dynamically imported dependency or tokenizer metadata file; per-file limitations remain explicit.
